title: Newly modelled allocations are reported leaked after a refused statement or a non-escaping return hands them on: 109 of 125 added leak leaves, 43 of 44 Unknown -> provisional Unsafe functions, 21 of 22 unit moves
why: Card W44-COLLECTION-ALLOCATION admits `v = ALLOC(... sizeof(*v) ...)`, so the destination is bound to the call's owned identity instead of being poisoned by the refused statement. Its arbiter (docs/reports/w44-collection-allocation/census/leak-attribution.txt, scripts/leak_attribution.py) adds 125 leak leaves on 46 functions (leak 271 -> 396), every one naming an allocation this card admitted. 107 are `handed-to-a-refused-statement`: the name reaches, after the allocation, a statement the classifier refuses (a list-insertion macro such as `TAILQ_INSERT_TAIL`, `rd_list_add(&conf->plugins, rkplug)`, a member store, an uncontracted callee); a refused statement withdraws the residual claim only for a publication the publication reader recognises (constraint 10, CTWIN-PUBLISH-INDIRECT) and spares every binding it cannot write (constraint 10a), so the identity stays owed to the exit. 2 are `returned-under-cast` (`return (rd_kafka_message_t *)rkm;`, `return rd_kafka_toppar_keep0(..., rktp);`), which the return route answers with no escaped place (constraint 5b). None of these 109 is witnessed; the functions read by hand (rd_kafka_coord_cache_add, rd_kafka_mock_handle_EndTxn, rd_kafka_plugin_new, rd_kafka_message_new) publish the object into a list or return it. The other 16 leaves are unit-test assertion-failure returns that do not free a fake `rk` (unittest_http_get_params_append, ut_sasl_oauthbearer_oidc_assertion_create), witnessed by reading the source. 43 of the 44 Unknown -> provisional Unsafe function moves and 21 of the 22 unit moves rest on unwitnessed claims only. Provisional Unsafe is not an upstream defect claim. DISCHARGE: a decision on the accusing arm for an identity handed to a refused statement or returned under a non-place spelling (withdraw the residual claim as an unresolved effect, as a recognised publication does; or keep it and witness each claim), with Lean parity and a measured re-pin of the leak pin; coordinate with W44-LEAK-PIN-AUDIT.

title: Dereference `sizeof` operands outside an ordinary call statement, member operands and two reader quirks keep their refusal
why: Card W44-COLLECTION-ALLOCATION admits `*NAME`, `**NAME` and `NAME[LITERAL]` operands (every declaration of NAME a pointer declarator with enough stars, no array dimension, a specifier never variably modified) only at the lexical access gate of a statement whose first call is an ordinary callee. It withdrew 204 of the census's 226 `indirect memory access` leaves whose line's only access is such an operand (224 on 211 Unknown functions at BEFORE). Still refused: (a) a statement with no ordinary call (`n = sizeof(*p);`, 4 at the census) and conditions and returns naming such an operand, which the fixed scalar type-query rule (type_query.rs) does not read; (b) member operands `sizeof(*p->q)` / `sizeof(p->q)` (100 and 122 occurrences; 21 owned-result allocations); (c) the declarator reader reads `( NAME * sizeof …` as a declaration candidate and refuses the whole function's declarations, so `x_alloc(n * sizeof(*p))` keeps its refusal (test `a_leading_multiplication_the_declaration_reader_refuses_keeps_the_refusal`); (d) protected-formal discovery reads `sizeof(*p) * n` as a dereference of a formal `n`, so the argument refuses as `call has an unmodeled formal address or borrowed expression`; (e) 5 of the 14 `T **` allocation candidates keep a refusal for another access on their line. 134 `indirect memory access` leaves remain within two lines of a dereference operand at AFTER (an upper bound; most carry another access). DISCHARGE: the type-query route widened to the same operand premise, member operands under the typed member reader, and the two reader quirks repaired, each with Lean parity and a measured re-pin.

title: The `C operator sizeof` family is a cast around a scalar query: 465 leaves, 398 of them `(T)(sizeof(NAME))`
why: The brief of card W44-COLLECTION-ALLOCATION pointed at the family `C operator \`sizeof\` requires type/operand analysis` (447 leaves on Unknown functions at the W43-INDEXED-RESOURCE-COLLECTIONS integration baseline). Its census (docs/reports/w44-collection-allocation/census/sizeof-census.txt) found it is not a dereference-operand family: 410 of the 447 sit on lines whose operand is a parenthesised name, and at AFTER 398 of the 465 leaves (355 on Unknown functions, 43 on provisional Unsafe) are librdkafka's `size_t __len2 = (size_t)(sizeof(_v));` macro expansion — a scalar query under a cast, which the fixed type-query rule (type_query.rs) replaces by its marker but `is_scalar_initializer` refuses for the cast. Only 1 Unknown function was blocked by this family alone at BEFORE (LZ4HC_rotatePattern). The card leaves it unchanged. DISCHARGE: a card admitting one leading scalar cast around an admitted type query in the scalar-initializer route (constraint 5a: the marker still never a value), with Lean parity and a measured re-pin.

title: 9 of the 14 `T **` array allocations are no longer refused (7 bind), and still no element operation decides under the collection rules
why: Card W44-COLLECTION-ALLOCATION's census found 14 self-referential dereference allocations into a `T **` destination; its admission withdrew the allocation refusal of 9, and 7 of those bind their destination (rd_kafka_conf_kv_split and rd_kafka_handle_ApiVersion reach another refusal; docs/reports/w44-collection-allocation/census/collection-reach.txt). Only one of those functions, rd_kafka_ListGroups_resp_cb, has an element operation the classifier lowers (`grps[i++] = rd_strndup(...)`, L24950), and its array does not resolve: `rd_malloc`'s result is nullable and the body never tests it, so `resolved_aggregate_owner` finds no non-null identity and the node is its fallback. The others fill their arrays through statements the element lowering does not take (call-argument accesses, named-pointer stores, member bounds). So 0 arrays became collections, 0 of the 27 recognised element operations moved, and 0 functions are Safe through collection element nodes. DISCHARGE: the first arbiter in which an admitted `T **` allocation's element operation resolves, measured alongside W43-INDIRECT-CALL-ARGUMENT-ACCESS, W43-COLLECTION-NAME-STORE and W43-COLLECTION-LOOP-SHAPES.
